issue.title: When multiple vehicles are connected, all systems get data from all vehicles, regardless of sysid.

comments.body:
> The documentation suggests that when you create a plugin (like Telemetry) for a system it will give you data just for that system. 

Yes it should do that.

Which version of MAVSDK are you using?
I am using the master/main branch as of October 20, 2023. On commit a9c198156722b26cbbcadfb148d01116deea4f2f.

And how did you establish that this commit from 2022 is responsible for this change? Did you manage to revert/fix it?

Maybe @julianoes has some insights about these changes, too.
Oh dear, did I break this? Thanks for reporting @poli0048!

Hi Jonas,

I think we are reading the code the same way - I agree with your assessment. It seems to me that there are two options:
1 - Revert to the previous architecture where void MavsdkImpl::receive_message() does sysid-based message routing, but then each system processes the messages it receives separately (and presumably invokes necessary callbacks).
2 - Modify the MavlinkMessageHandler class so that when callbacks are registered, the sysid of the registering system is recorded in the callback table, then only pass messages to systems if the callback was registered with the same sysid as the incoming message.

I am still getting familiar with MAVSDK and I don't know the reasons for the changes that were previously made here, so I can't say which approach is necessarily better, but I think either strategy could resolve this issue.

I would tend to go for 2. @julianoes do you have an opinion on that?

@poli0048 would you be willing to try fixing it (once we agree with Julian on what would be the way to go)?
If you would both prefer that I take a crack at fixing it I can try. I will wait for Julian to weigh in.
I'm looking into it now. You're spot on, and I don't quite remember my thinking back then either... and I'm also tending to 2.
@poli0048 can you try https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2192 and check if it fixes the problem? That would be great!
Sorry for just doing it but it bugged me enough that I wanted to do it rightaway.
Looks like I broke the tests...

I first tried 2. but it turns out that didn't work for commands. The reason was that the initial system gets initialized with target 0. At that point the MavlinkCommandSender registers for any messages, in this case for 0. Then, once a system is discovered, the system ID is set to 1 but the MavlinkCommandSender's subscription is still 0, and it doesn't receive the acks.

I therefore went back to 1, so we now have MavlinkMessageHandlers in MavsdkImpl for components and in SystemImpl for systems.

I know this issue is closed now but I wanted to follow up - I have just tested the changes you made and it does seem to resolve the issue for me. I can connect to two drones now and the messages are properly separated by system. Thank you for taking the time to fix this!
Awesome, thanks for the feedback @poli0048 and raising this blunder in the first place!

issue.title: core: fix incoming messages by sysid

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
This fixes a recent regression after a refactoring where messages from different systems are no longer filtered according to the source system ID and instead are distributed to all systems.

Fixes #2191.
